extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate mathematics students and instructors learning proof-writing / mathematical reasoning
extracted.subtask_description: Instructional material aimed at developing students' ability to construct and write mathematical proofs and to learn the process of doing mathematics alongside relevant mathematical topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to construct and write mathematical proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the main goals of this book is to help you to develop the ability to construct and write mathematical proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on acquiring the skill of producing correct, well-structured proofs rather than only learning isolated results; the book is designed to teach proof construction as an explicit learning outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the process of doing mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: This book is not just about mathematical content but is also about the process of doing mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should learn how mathematicians think and work (problem-solving approaches, ways of developing arguments), not merely memorize statements; the pedagogy emphasizes process skills alongside content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of important mathematical topics to support future study
rubrics_metrics.description: Along the way, you will also learn some important mathematical topics that will help you in your future study of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content selection is intended to provide background and examples that reinforce proof skills and prepare students for further coursework; mastery of these topics supports successful proof-writing.
